To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SMESE is an ontology based semantic metadata enrichment software system for multi platform digital libraries.

SMESE can be used for metadata driven applications in digital libraries, and SMESE can be applied to any metadata driven software ecosystem, and SMESE supports multi platform and multi product software development.
SMESE is an ontology mapping based semantic metadata enrichment software ecosystems to support multi platform digital library metadata driven applications.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMESE is a semantic digital library software ecosystem based on a metadata model for digital library interoperability and enrichment.
SMESE is a SPLE approach that supports the creation of a semantic digital library by integrating metadata driven applications.
SMESE is a semantic digital library ecosystem which supports the development of multi platform metadata driven digital libraries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SMESE is the first SPLE process to support metadata driven applications and to provide a decision support for dynamic reconfiguration.
SMESE has the potential to become a new paradigm for the software ecosystem development.
SMESE is a SPLE based software ecosystem that aggregates, enriches, synchronizes and presents metadata from multiple metadata sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed SMESE is a generic software ecosystem which can be used to support multi platform digital library applications.
SMESE can be used as a reference model for building metadata based software ecosystems.
